@appName.description: The app's name, as the interface shows it.

aDestinationIsNotADomain: A destination is not a domain, an IP address or a range.
aDomainAnIpAddressOr: A domain, an IP address or a URL
afterARestartRouteAgainIf: After a restart, route again if it was on.
warnVpn: Another VPN ({iface}) carries all traffic: connections no rule matches still go through it.
anotherVpnOrNetworkToolHolds: Another VPN or network tool holds the routes Pith needs.

@endRulesChanged.description: Beside the interface of a connection in Activity that Pith closed because the rules changed, so that its app reconnects under the new rules. Not a failure. Lowercase, like "backup".

closedWhenTheRulesChanged: Closed when the rules changed, for the app to reconnect under the new ones
blockRulesAlwaysWinOtherwiseThe: Block rules always win; otherwise the first matching rule from the top decides. Drag to reorder.
canTConnectNoInterfaceOf: Can't connect: no interface of its rule is up
connectToAHostAndPort: Connect to a host and port through each interface, to compare them.
ifTheMacLosesTheInternet: If the Mac loses the internet right after routing starts, undo it.
includesItsSubdomainsClickForThis: Includes its subdomains: click for this domain alone
warnInterfaceDown: Not connected: {names}. Rules that use them try their next interface.
itNeverReadsWhatAppsSend: It never reads what apps send: no decryption, nothing uploaded.
itOnlyRoutesWhileYouTurn: It only routes while you turn routing on.
itsRuleSFirstInterfaceDidn: Its rule's first interface didn't connect
deleteSceneBody: {count, plural, =0 {It has no rules.} one {Its rule goes with it.} other {Its # rules go with it.}}
leaveEmptyForEveryAppAn: Leave empty for every app. An app's helpers and the system services that work for it match too.
macosSendsConnectionsNoRuleMatches: macOS sends connections no rule matches here
newMatchingConnectionsAreRefusedConnecti: New matching connections are refused. Connections already open stay.
noRuleMatchedTheSystemS: No rule matched: the system's network
noRuleMatchesTheSystemS: no rule matches: the system's routing
noneOfItsRuleSInterfaces: None of its rule's interfaces connected
notADomainIpAddressOr: Not a domain, IP address or range
notInstalledRoutingNeedsItMacos: Not installed. Routing needs it; macOS asks for your password once.
testToSeeItsPublicIp: Test to see its public IP

@testToSeeItsPublicIp.description: On an interface's card before it has been tested, beside the Test button, which measures its latency and finds its public IP.

onlyWhatPithRoutedTheBytes: Only what Pith routed: the bytes apps sent and received, without the network's own overhead.
pithRoutesConnectionsWithASmall: Pith routes connections with a small helper that runs with administrator rights. macOS asks for your password once to install it.
pithSavesNothingOverTheFile: Pith saves nothing over the file until you decide.
pithWaitsInTheMenuBar: Pith waits in the menu bar.
readTheHostNameAppsConnect: Read the host name apps connect to (TLS SNI, HTTP Host), so domain rules match. Contents stay unread.
recognizingDomainsIsOffSoDomain: Recognizing domains is off, so domain rules may not match.
routingCutTheInternetSoPith: Routing cut the internet, so Pith undid it.
routingIsOffThisPageShows: Routing is off. This page shows the connections Pith routes.
otherSceneRunning: Routing runs by “{scene}”. These rules apply once you switch.
scenesRulesInterfaceNamesAndSettings: Scenes, rules, interface names and settings, in one file.
seeWhereAConnectionWouldGo: See where a connection would go
testsConnectThroughOneInterfaceAt: Tests connect through one interface at a time, whatever the rules say.
replaceBackupBody: {count, plural, one {The backup has # scene.} other {The backup has # scenes.}}
thisDomainAloneClickToInclude: This domain alone: click to include its subdomains
triedFromTheTopTheNext: Tried from the top: the next one when one can't connect.
turnOnToInstallTheHelper: Turn on to install the helper
whenNoneOfThemConnectsUse: When none of them connects, use the system's network
whenNoneOfTheseConnectThe: When none of these connect, the connection goes as macOS routes it
youCanRemoveItInSettings: You can remove it in Settings at any time.

@listComma.description: Between the items of a list, before the last.

@listAnd.description: A list's items before the last, joined by listComma, and its last.

@appsAndMore.description: A rule's first two apps, then how many more it has.

@targetsAndMore.description: A rule's first two destinations, then how many more it has.

@windowTitle.description: The main window's title, and the menu bar icon's tooltip.

@openPithMenu.description: The item of the menu bar icon's menu that opens the window.

@helperInstalled.description: The helper's state in a word, in Settings: installed and answering. Its version follows.

@helperNotInstalled.description: The helper's state in a word, in Settings.

@helperOutdated.description: The helper's state in a word, in Settings: it doesn't match this version of the app and must be updated.

@cantVerifyHelper.description: The routing state in the window's corner, the panel and Settings when Pith can't confirm the installed helper is the one it ships. Not a stopped state.

pithCanTVerifyItsHelper: Pith can't confirm the installed helper is the one it ships, so it won't use it. Reinstall the helper in Settings, or reinstall Pith.

@pithCanTVerifyItsHelper.description: A notice, an error and a tooltip when Pith can't verify its helper. Pith neither uses it nor asks for a password by itself.

@reinstall.description: A button in Settings that installs the helper again, replacing one Pith can't verify. macOS asks for an administrator's password.

itDoesnTMatchThisVersion: It doesn't match this version of Pith. Update it to route.

@itDoesnTMatchThisVersion.description: Tooltip of the helper's state in Settings when it must be replaced to match this version of the app.

@helperNotAnsweringState.description: The routing state in the window's corner and the panel when the installed helper doesn't answer. What it routes is unknown, so not a stopped state.

theHelperIsnTAnswering: The helper isn't answering. Pith keeps trying; if it doesn't come back, repair it in Settings.

@theHelperIsnTAnswering.description: A notice and error message when the installed helper doesn't answer. Try Again asks at once, without a password.

@repair.description: A button in Settings that sets the helper up again when it doesn't answer. macOS asks for an administrator's password.

@helperNotAnswering.description: The helper's state in a word, in Settings: installed, but it does not answer. Its version follows.

@mitLicense.description: The app's license, under its name and version in Settings › About.

macosAsksForYourPassword: macOS will ask for your administrator password.

@macosAsksForYourPassword.description: The one line of the prompt to install or update the helper.

@targetPlaceholderShort.description: The placeholder of the rule editor's field that adds destinations.

@warnVpnShort.description: A notice, short; warnVpn says it whole, on hover.

@warnInterfaceDownShort.description: A notice, short: interfaces rules use that are down. warnInterfaceDown says it whole, on hover.

@recognizingDomainsIsOff.description: A notice, short; recognizingDomainsIsOffSoDomain says it whole, on hover.

helperPromptInstall: Pith needs your password to install its routing helper.
helperPromptUpdate: Pith needs your password to update its routing helper.
helperPromptUninstall: Pith needs your password to remove its routing helper.

@helperPromptInstall.description: What macOS's administrator password dialog says when Pith installs its helper.

@changeHotspotIp.description: Button on a mobile hotspot's card: the hotspot reconnects to its carrier, which gives it new public addresses.

@hotspotPassword.description: Title of the sheet that asks for a hotspot's admin password, and tooltip of the lock on its card.

@ipUnchanged.description: After changing a hotspot's IP, when its public IP stayed the same.

theHotspotRefusedItsPassword: The hotspot refused its admin password.

@localProxies.description: The title of the settings' group of local SOCKS5 proxies, each a port on this Mac going out through one interface.

socks5OnThisMacOnly: SOCKS5 for apps on this Mac, without a password. Each port goes out through its interface alone, and fails while that isn't connected.

@socks5OnThisMacOnly.description: Under the local proxies, beside Add Proxy: what they are.

@addProxy.description: Button: adds a local proxy on the next free port, through a connected interface.

@doubleClickToChangeThePort.description: Tooltip of a local proxy's address, 127.0.0.1:1080.

@proxyOff.description: A local proxy that is turned off.

@portInUse.description: A local proxy that can't listen: another program holds its port.

@itsInterfaceIsnTConnected.description: A local proxy whose interface is unplugged or down: its connections fail rather than use another interface.

itsInterfaceHasNoDns: Its interface has no DNS server

@itsInterfaceHasNoDns.description: A local proxy whose interface has no DNS server: it can reach IP addresses, not names.

@proxyListening.description: A local proxy that is taking connections; followed by its open connections and bytes.

@proxyStarting.description: A local proxy turned on that isn't listening yet.

useAPortFrom1024To65535: Use a port from 1024 to 65535 that no other proxy uses.

@useAPortFrom1024To65535.description: Shown when a local proxy's new port is out of range or taken by another proxy.
